learn.many.title: {count} gates at once
learn.H.title: Superposition
learn.H.body: Sends {q} from |0⟩ to an equal mix of |0⟩ and |1⟩, and from |1⟩ to the same mix with a minus sign. Applying H again undoes it.
learn.X.title: A bit flip
learn.X.body: Swaps the |0⟩ and |1⟩ parts of {q}, like a classical NOT.
learn.Y.title: Bit and phase flip
learn.Y.body: Flips {q} like X and also shifts the phase: |0⟩ becomes i|1⟩ and |1⟩ becomes −i|0⟩.
learn.Z.title: A phase flip
learn.Z.body: Changes the sign of the |1⟩ part of {q}. The probabilities stay the same, but the sign matters when parts of the state interfere later.
learn.S.title: Quarter-turn phase
learn.S.body: Multiplies the |1⟩ part of {q} by i: a quarter turn around the Z axis.
learn.Sdg.title: Undoing S
learn.Sdg.body: Multiplies the |1⟩ part of {q} by −i: a quarter turn back around the Z axis.
learn.T.title: Eighth-turn phase
learn.T.body: Multiplies the |1⟩ part of {q} by e^(iπ/4): an eighth of a turn around the Z axis.
learn.Tdg.title: Undoing T
learn.Tdg.body: Multiplies the |1⟩ part of {q} by e^(−iπ/4): an eighth of a turn back around the Z axis.
learn.P.title: Phase turn
learn.P.body: Multiplies the |1⟩ part of {q} by e^(i·{angle}): a turn of {angle} around the Z axis.
learn.RX.title: Rotation around X
learn.RX.body: Turns {q} by {angle} around the X axis of the Bloch sphere.
learn.RY.title: Rotation around Y
learn.RY.body: Turns {q} by {angle} around the Y axis of the Bloch sphere.
learn.RZ.title: Rotation around Z
learn.RZ.body: Turns {q} by {angle} around the Z axis of the Bloch sphere.
learn.CNOT.title: A conditional flip
learn.CZ.title: Conditional phase flip
learn.CZ.body: Changes the sign of the part of the state where {a} and {b} are both 1. It works the same whichever qubit you call the control.
learn.SWAP.title: Swap
learn.CCX.title: Double-controlled flip
learn.CCX.body: Flips {t} only when {c1} and {c2} are both 1.
learn.M.title: Measurement
learn.M.body: Reads {q} out as 0 or 1. Instead of picking one result at random, Qanvas shows how likely each one is, using the state just before measuring.
learn.entangled.one: {q} is now entangled, so its Bloch arrow shrinks: its state can no longer be described on its own.
learn.entangled.other: {q} are now entangled, so their Bloch arrows shrink: their states can no longer be described on their own.
learn.unchanged: This step didn't change the state.
learn.globalPhase: Only the global phase changed. No measurement can tell the difference.
bloch.title: Each qubit on its own
learn.RESET.title: Reset
learn.RESET.body: Puts {q} back to |0⟩, whatever it was. If {q} was entangled with other qubits, they're left as a mix of outcomes.
learn.condition: It only runs if {q} was measured as {value}.
learn.measuredMix: From here on, Qanvas keeps both possible results, each with its probability, so the next steps show what happens in either case.
results.noAmplitudes: After a measurement partway through, the state is a mix of possible outcomes, so there's no single list of amplitudes. The chart shows how likely each outcome is.
results.densityLimit: Measuring partway through and resetting work with up to {max} qubits in the browser. Remove qubits to see the results.
bloch.hintMixed: The arrow shows each qubit's state. It shrinks when the qubit is entangled with others, or when a measurement left its value uncertain.
bloch.hint: The arrow shows each qubit's state. It shrinks when the qubit is entangled with others.
bloch.description: {qubit}: {status}. Arrow at x {x}, y {y}, z {z}, length {length}.
code.label: Code
examples.title: Examples
examples.intro: Pick a circuit to explore. You can change it freely; undo takes you back.
examples.empty.name: Empty circuit
examples.empty.description: Start again from three empty wires.
tryThis.title: Try this
example.bell.name: Bell state
example.bell.description: Two entangled qubits that always agree when measured: 00 or 11, each half the time.
example.bell.tryThis: Delete the CNOT. Do q0 and q1 still always agree?
example.ghz.name: GHZ state
example.ghz.description: Three entangled qubits: you get 000 or 111, never a mix.
example.ghz.tryThis: Move the H gate after the first CNOT. Does q1 still follow q0?
example.superdense-coding.name: Superdense coding
example.superdense-coding.description: Sends two classical bits by sending one qubit of a shared Bell pair. Here the message is 11, written with X and Z.
example.superdense-coding.tryThis: Delete the Z gate. Which two bits arrive now?
example.teleportation.name: Quantum teleportation
example.teleportation.description: Moves the state of q0 onto q2 using a shared Bell pair. Qanvas can't act on measurement results yet, so the corrections use controlled gates instead.
example.teleportation.tryThis: Change the angle of the Ry gate on q0. Does q2's Bloch arrow follow it?
example.deutsch-jozsa.name: Deutsch–Jozsa
example.deutsch-jozsa.description: Tells in one run whether a function is constant or balanced. This one is balanced, so q0 and q1 never read 00.
example.deutsch-jozsa.tryThis: Delete both CNOTs to make the function constant. What do q0 and q1 read now?
example.grover-2.name: Grover search, 2 qubits
example.grover-2.description: Finds the marked item among four in a single round. The first CZ marks 11.
example.grover-2.tryThis: Put an X gate on q0 right before and right after the first CZ. Which item is found now?

download.title: Download
download.intro: Save the circuit as a notebook or a script that runs it and counts the outcomes, or as OpenQASM.
download.qasmHint: Just the circuit, in a format most quantum tools can open.
download.notebookIntro: Made with [Qanvas](https://ethan-rivas.github.io/qanvas/), in {framework}. Run each cell with Shift + Enter.
download.runIntro: Run the circuit {shots} times and count each outcome. Outcomes list the measured qubits with q0 first, like Qanvas.
download.measureAll: The circuit has no measurements, so every qubit is measured.
download.qiskitReverse: Qiskit puts classical bit 0 last in its bitstrings; reversing them puts q0 first, like Qanvas.
download.pyqvm: pyQuil's built-in simulator. In quantum-lab, "{qubits}q-qvm" uses the lab's QVM instead.

aer.topOutcomes: Showing the {shown} most frequent of {total} outcomes seen.
aer.timeout: Qiskit Aer took longer than {seconds} seconds, so the run was stopped.
aer.unreachable: Couldn't reach quantum-lab. Check that the lab is running, then try again.

aer.footer: Runs on Qiskit Aer in quantum-lab
